mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent upward trend (less negative) over the past four weeks, indicating a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue over the next four weeks, driving further increases.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility in the most recent week, reversing a prior decline, indicates a renewed return to offices that will boost weekday retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 14 days following a week where WORKPLACES increased by more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in TRANSIT mobility suggests people are spending less time at home and utilizing public transport more, driving increased out-of-home activities including retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL falling and TRANSIT rising in the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive growth in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, often a leading indicator of general economic activity, suggests increasing confidence and out-of-home movement that will spill over into RETAIL_REC within the next week, especially during a reopening phase.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 7 days, even when GROCERY_PHARM shows sustained positive growth over the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As summer progresses, increased outdoor activity reflected in PARKS mobility, even with some fluctuation, indicates a general trend of people being out and about, which will indirectly boost nearby retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite PARKS mobility showing an upward trend over the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility were to sharply increase, reversing its recent downward trend, it would signal a return to staying at home, negatively impacting out-of-home activities like retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite a week-on-week increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility of more than 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility would indicate a significant reduction in commuting and general movement, leading to a decrease in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Given the current context of reopening, the general upward trend across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) suggests a broad recovery in public life and economic activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing an upward trend over the preceding four weeks.
